body.x: NTREX (President Sang-Hyuk Oh, www.rexbot3d.com) revealed RexBot3D OC-120, an easily-installed and user-friendly 3D printer, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

RexBot3D OC-120 boasts high quality and durability with its metal work frame for a competitive price, and even beginners can easily familiarize themselves with this printer’s software. Also, advanced precision assures top quality, while MDF case allows easy assembly.

This printer can be conveniently installed anywhere, thanks to its slim and simple design. Additionally, its printing method with auto-leveling via proximity sensor and core XY system allows easy replacement of the heater and nozzle sizes and memory card slots makes it possible to print without a connection to a PC.

The MoonWalker, also presented at the tradeshow, is a motor controller that controls electric current, speed, and position and thus can be utilized for a wide range of purposes, from research for a robot arm, a moving robot, and industrial machinery to everyday life.

The device supports digital in/out port and analog/pulse input port and provides a PC program with simple configuration and usage. It supports scripts which enables the usage of internal variable, operating commands, and external IO, and the internal variable can be monitored when using the script.

Up to 255 Device IDs can be created for multi-drop connection with CAN communications, while serial communication and analog/pulse input instructions can be given simultaneously. Functions such as battery voltage measurement, overvoltage/undervoltage protection, and monitor’s electric current and overcurrent measurement all come with this product.

NTREX is currently unfolding diverse operations, including electronic parts trade, field sales, foreign market establishment, and on/off line distribution and sales of electronic parts, while primarily concentrating on the growing power industry of 3D printers, robot development, and embedded system R&D.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
